text:
maya: Heads up — since the scheduler tweak last night we've been seeing ~2x TTFT P95 on a few low-concurrency routes (customer-facing chat endpoints). Not a sustained throughput drop, more like spikes during warm-up windows.

liam: Link? graphs?

maya: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/serving/ttft-breakdown?panel=route&var-route=chat-small
P95 went from 85ms -> 180ms for /v1/chat on eu-west1 between 02:10-02:25. CPU/GPU Util steady.

nora: I replayed a few requests locally against the new scheduler and added verbose prefetch logs — looks like KV prefetcher is firing too aggressively and evicting entries mid-handshake. Logs show repeated prefetch miss+evict cycles: 
```
[kv_prefetch] route=chat-small req_id=abc123 prefetched_keys=64 hit=0 evicted=12 ttl_ms=120
[kv_prefetch] route=chat-small req_id=abc123 prefetched_keys=32 hit=0 evicted=32 ttl_ms=30
```
That aligns with the TTFT spikes when the microbatch handshake stretches.

devex: Oof. We currently attribute TTFT -> 'queue' vs 'decode' vs 'kv' in dashboards, but we don't have kernel-level attributions or per-token kernel_id on traces. Could be hard to tell if kernel selection (microkernel vs full) or KV churn is the culprit.

perf-bot: Sample profiler (hotpath):
```
0.42s  kernel_launch (microkernel_v2)
0.11s  kv_cache_lookup
0.09s  memcpy_h2d
0.38s  kernel_launch (full_kernel)
```
Notable: repeated kernel_launch entries interleaved with kv lookups.

liam: Can we add a small instrumentation patch: tag every generated token event with fields: `kernel_id`, `batch_size_at_launch`, `kvcache_hit` (y/n), and `handshake_ts`? If we store that on the token timeline we can roll up per-route distributions and correlate TTFT slices to kernel launches.

nora: Yes — and capture microbatch handshake durations as two timestamps: `enqueue_ts` and `launch_ts` so we can compute handshake latency per-batch. Also add `kvcache_prefetch_count` per-request. Minimal storage: only sample 1% of tokens by default.

devex: Proposed dashboard panels: 
- Token-level waterfall: stacked breakdown (enqueue -> handshake -> kernel_launch -> decode) with kernel_id coloring.
- Kernel churn heatmap: axis=(route, kernel_id) value=token_count where churn = frequent kernel switches per-request.
- KV prefetch churn: time-series for `prefetch_count` and `eviction_rate` by route.

liam: Quick query draft for rollup (prometheus-ish pseudo):
```
sum(rate(token_latency_bucket{stage="kernel_launch",route=~"chat-.*"}[5m])) by (route,kernel_id)
```
We might need a dedicated index in our trace DB for `kernel_id` since it's high-cardinality.

perf-bot: Suggestion: sample at 5% for suspect routes (chat-small, chat-medium) and 0.1% for others to reduce index pressure. Also compress kernel_id -> small int.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: deploy started by @nora: infra/scheduler-tweak-revert + token-instr-probe (canary) -> canary: eu-west1-2 (6 hosts)

nora: I'll push a canary instrumentation build that emits the extra token fields and prefetch counters sampled at 5% for chat routes. Will also add a toggle `env.SAMPLE_KV_TELEMETRY` so we can flip live.

maya: For immediate triage: can we replay a 10k request sample with the revert + instrumentation and produce a heatmap? If kernel churn is visible there we can decide whether to revert permanently.

liam: I'll run the replay on a dedicated test harness and upload the token waterfall CSV. Expect ~30m to finish.

devex: Action items: 
- nora: land canary instrumentation + sample toggle (ETA: today EOD)
- liam: run replay and produce waterfall/heatmap (ETA: +1h after canary)
- maya: prepare alert rule to fire if per-route kernel_switches/sec > 0.5 for 5m (to catch regressions)

maya: Also — don't forget to tag the trace samples with `route_version` so we can correlate to rollout. Last time we saw this it was a version alignment issue between scheduler + kernel selector.

nora: noted. I'll include `route_version` and `scheduler_commit` in sample payload.

liam: Uploading partial replay results here when done. If anyone wants to pair on interpreting the waterfall ping me.

maya: Thanks all. If the canary shows KV churn as root cause we revert the scheduler tweak and iterate on prefetch heuristics (limit concurrent prefetches per-route). :thumbsup:
